newsitem.title: USA: Boehner concerned House Republicans taped discussion.
newsitem.headline: Boehner concerned House Republicans taped discussion.

text.p: Republican unity in the House of Representatives will be in peril if members have decided to tape-record party caucuses, a member of House Speaker Newt Gingrich's leadership team warned Thursday in a letter to colleagues.

In the letter, John Boehner of Ohio, No 4 in leadership, said he had learned that some news reporters had obtained a tape from Wednesday's "family conversation" among Republicans over a thwarted move to depose Gingrich.

"I find myself hoping that this incident can be attributed to the acute interests of the media instead of the more troubling possibility -- that a member of our conference may have taped part of our proceedings," Boehner wrote.

"Republican Conference meetings should be a place where members speak their mind(s) and where we can have honest, pointed discussions ... But if a member were to take the incredible step of taping his colleague's words to be used in the news media, it would seriously threaten the openness, the trust and the good will we have all agreed to try and foster among Republicans in the House."
During the three-hour meeting Wednesday, Republicans closed ranks behind leaders and one of Gingrich's top deputies apologised for missteps that emboldened dissidents.
